qs.q: What is the primary underlying cause of an endemic goiter in patients experiencing iodine deficiency?
o: Autoimmune destruction of thyroid follicular cells
Benign localized tumor growth within the gland
Constant TSH stimulation causing glandular enlargement
qs.e: Iodine deficiency leads to endemic goiter as the thyroid gland enlarges under constant TSH stimulation to capture trace iodine. Autoimmune destruction is characteristic of Hashimoto's disease rather than simple dietary deficiency.

qs.q: Iodine deficiency goiter causes thyroid enlargement because
o: Iodine directly stimulates thyroid follicular cell proliferation.
Autoantibodies activate TSH receptors, leading to gland enlargement.
Reduced T3/T4 levels raise TSH, causing follicular hyperplasia and hypertrophy.
Decreased calcitonin production triggers thyroid cell proliferation.
qs.e: Most common cause of goiter worldwide = iodine deficiency. Treatment: iodine supplementation. Endemic goiter = affects >10% of a population.
